# RedRouter: Video Generation

Requires `RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL` and, when the instance requires one, `RED_ROUTER_API_KEY`. See
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reddb-io/red-router/main/skills/red-router/SKILL.md for setup.

## Discover

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/videos/generations
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" "$RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/models/info?id=<model-id>"
```

`GET /v1/videos/generations` lists the video models this key can use.

## Two flows

Video generation is slow, so RedRouter offers a blocking call and a job-based call.

| Endpoint | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/videos/generations` | Blocks and returns the finished result in the response |
| `POST /v1/videos/generations` with header `Prefer: respond-async` | Submits an xAI Grok Imagine job and returns a request id |
| `POST /v1/videos/edits` | Submits an xAI job that edits an existing video (always async) |
| `POST /v1/videos/extensions` | Submits an xAI job that extends an existing video (always async) |
| `GET /v1/videos/{request_id}` | Polls an async job |

The async flow needs a connected xAI account in the RedRouter dashboard, either an xAI API key or
a Grok sign-in. Whether a subscription includes video quota is decided by xAI; an upstream
permission error means the connected account has no video access.

## Request fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | yes for the blocking flow | `provider/model` id from discovery; the async flow always uses `xai/grok-imagine-video` |
| `prompt` | yes for text-to-video | video description |
| `duration` | no | seconds |
| `aspect_ratio` | no | for example `16:9` or `9:16` |
| `resolution` | no | for example `720p` |
| `image` | no | `{ "url": "https://... or data:image/...;base64,..." }` for image-to-video |
| `video` | edits and extensions | `{ "url": "https://....mp4" }` |

Fields the async flow does not use are forwarded to xAI as sent. Check xAI's video API reference
for the full list.

## Examples

Blocking call:

```bash
curl -X POST $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/videos/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"<model-id>","prompt":"A cinematic tracking shot through a neon city at night"}'
```

Async job (submit, then poll):

```bash
curl -X POST $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/videos/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Prefer: respond-async" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"model":"xai/grok-imagine-video","prompt":"A cinematic tracking shot through a neon city at night","duration":8,"aspect_ratio":"16:9","resolution":"720p"}'
# returns {"request_id":"...","status":"pending"}

curl $RED_ROUTER_BASE_URL/v1/videos/<request_id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RED_ROUTER_API_KEY"
# pending or processing, then done with {"video":{"url":"https://....mp4"}}, or failed
```

Download the file from `video.url` once the status is `done`.

## Notes

- A job is bound to the connection that created it; polling always uses that same connection.
  To pin creation to a specific connection, send its id in an `x-connection-id` request header.
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on creation. Creation is never retried automatically, because a
  retry could create and bill two videos. Reusing a key with a different body returns 409.
- A status of `uncertain` means the submission could not be confirmed; do not resubmit blindly.
